children: CBOT grain futures turned lower in afternoon trading, with fund traders moving cautiously. "I think it's all money flow," says Karl Setzer of Consus Ag Consulting. "Nobody wants to extend the market too far in either direction." Analysts say that the back-and-forth between traders buying on breaks and farmers selling into rallies is keeping the market stable. Most-active CBOT corn futures are down 0.2%, while soybeans slide 0.3% and wheat falls 0.3%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
